output.reason: Localized itchy blistery rash on both forearms after reported poison ivy exposure, with fever and breathing trouble denied, can be managed with OTC measures and clear escalation triggers.
output.patientMessage: You can start self-care now: OTC hydrocortisone or calamine, cool compresses, and an OTC antihistamine for itch; ask your pharmacist what suits you. Poison ivy rash typically follows contact and can appear to spread for days. Message a clinician here if the rash reaches your face or genitals, covers large areas, or becomes painful, warm or pus-filled; seek urgent care for fever, facial swelling or breathing trouble.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy)
Secondary skin infection if the area becomes painful/warm

redFlags.concern: Extent of body surface involved beyond forearms
Pain, warmth or purulence suggesting infection

output.vitalSigns: No vital sign values reported; fever denied by report, but no temperature reading or measurement method is stated.
output.evidenceLimitations: Extent of body surface and whether face/genitals are involved are unreported, so severity-based systemic treatment eligibility is unresolved.
